subject: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE function
notes:
REFUTER PASS. VERDICT RETAINED AT DIVERGES, with the crash window widened as on AR-15.48.3-4 and one piece of the adjudicator's positive evidence independently re-derived from the spec rather than accepted.

CITATION RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.48.3 "If argument-1 is a combined date and time format, the contents of argument-2 shall be a valid combined date and time in that format." -> OK (§15.48.3 5)).

THE TIME PORTION IS GENUINELY VALIDATED, and I checked the two subtle legs against the spec text rather than trusting the comments. §15.3.3.2 says of the BASIC common time format with fractional seconds that "the decimal separator does not appear in the data", and of the EXTENDED form that "the two colon characters and the decimal separator appear in the data" - Tokenize's `bool extended = fmt.IndexOf(':') >= 0 || fmt.IndexOf('-') >= 0;` and its `segs.Add(new(false, default, 0, c, extended))` for '.'/',' implement exactly that split, and Annex D.31.5.8's own worked data "19950215T05142781+0500" (no '.' present, against the format "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm") corroborates it. §15.3.3.3 gives hour 00..23, minute 00..59 and seconds ">= 00 and < 60 when the LEAP-SECOND directive with the OFF phrase is in effect" - Analyze's (0,23)/(0,59)/(0,59) match under the only mode this compiler supports. The mandatory 'T' (§15.3.3.7) and the 'Z' marker (§15.3.3.5) are in-data separator segments that must appear; the offset sign is restricted to '+'/'-'/'0' with §15.3.3.6.1's zero-sign-implies-zero-magnitude narrowing; offset hour 0..23 and offset minute 0..59; and the trailing `pos != data.Length` check bars a short or over-long argument-2. An error position becomes EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError.

THE DEFECT is inherited from the date half and is reachable through THIS rule on its own: DateTimeFormatGrammar#Describe classifies "YYYYWwwDThhmmss" as Combined (BasicDates contains "YYYYWwwD" and ZoneOfWidth accepts the basic "hhmmss"), so it passes the §15.48.3 r2 screen, and argument-2 "9999W526T235959" OR "9999W527T235959" satisfies every range check before Analyze reaches `ISOWeek.ToDateTime(9999, 52, ...)`. Both reconstruct past DateTime.MaxValue (10000-01-01 and 10000-01-02 - the two-day window I recomputed on AR-15.48.3-4; the adjudicator recorded only the second) and throw System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException, where §15.3 rule 14 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result. SAME ROOT CAUSE as AR-15.48.3-4 and the landed AR-15.79.3-5; ONE fix closes all three, so do not triple-count.

SECOND, WEAKER POINT, retained because it bars any CONFORMS reading and names the fix's right shape: for THIS function the integer date is the only thing needed (§15.48.4's NOTE), yet Analyze builds it unconditionally - which is precisely what makes a purely time-side question fault on a date-side computation.

test-ref EMPTY, and the gap is TOTAL - I grepped tests/ for every use of the name: no test, golden or corpus program passes a COMBINED format to INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE at all, so neither the accept nor the reject side of this rule is exercised anywhere. Annex D.31.5.8's own worked example ("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500" -> 143951, which I verified arithmetically: 1995-02-15 is 143,951 days inclusive from the 1601-01-01 epoch) is the obvious fixture and is absent.

EDITIONS from the standard (Annex E carries no occurrence of the name), not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.
